subject: Architecture & perf deep-dive: confirm time and prep items
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.ai>
To: Paul Nguyen <paul.nguyen@bridgeworks.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 18 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Architecture & perf deep-dive: confirm time and prep items

Hi Paul —

Thanks again for the interest in Redwood. Per our call last week, we want to split the session into two parts: (1) a short product demo (20m) and (2) a technical deep-dive focused on performance targets, load-test plan, and deployment architecture (40–50m).

Proposed slots (PDT):
- Tue Apr 20 10:00–11:15 (PDT)
- Wed Apr 21 08:30–09:45 (PDT) — earlier for your APAC colleagues

Agenda (attached: Agenda_v1.pdf):
- 0–20m: demo and feature highlights (Laura)
- 20–80m: architecture walkthrough (Marcus) and perf targets + load-test plan (Karthik)
- 80–90m: Q&A and next steps, mutual action plan

Before we lock the slot, two quick asks to help Marcus and Karthik prepare:
1) What steady-state token throughput and p95 latency targets should we validate for your app (typical window size / context length)?
2) Will you want Redwood to run an in-service load test against a staging endpoint, or do you prefer a synthetic run we host in our environment? For in-service runs we usually need a short IP allowlist and a test key.

If you confirm one of the slots and send your preferred targets (a line or two is fine), we’ll assign resources and circulate the runbook.

Thanks,
Olga
Olga Petrov
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
olga@redwood.ai
https://redwood.ai

Attachment: Agenda_v1.pdf (PDF, 2 pages)
From: Paul Nguyen <paul.nguyen@bridgeworks.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.ai>
Cc: eng@bridgeworks.com
Date: Sun, 18 Apr 2027 18:05:12 +0000
Subject: Re: Architecture & perf deep-dive: confirm time and prep items

Thanks Olga — Tue Apr 20 10:00 PDT works best for our core team. We27ll have two engineers (Me and Saira) attend; Saira is in India (IST) so the Wed early slot would be tougher.

Quick answers to your prep Qs:
- Target: steady 500 tokens/sec per instance (our normal generation profile ~400–700 tokens per request), target p95 generation latency <= 150ms for 1k token window. We27re particularly sensitive to tail latency when cache misses occur.
- Run type: we prefer Redwood to run a synthetic load test in your staging environment first. If that looks good we27ll consider an in-service smoke test. For the synthetic run we can share a small sample prompt set and a mimic traffic trace.

Attached a short CSV with example target distributions.

Paul
Paul Nguyen
Eng Manager, BridgeWorks
paul.nguyen@bridgeworks.com
Attachment: perf_targets.csv (CSV, 1KB)

From: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.ai>
To: Paul Nguyen <paul.nguyen@bridgeworks.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 19 Apr 2027 02:40:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Architecture & perf deep-dive: confirm time and prep items

Paul — thanks, Tue Apr 20 10:00 PDT is locked. Invites sent to the addresses you shared.

Marcus / Karthik: please own the perf deep-dive and synthetic load run prep. Key asks from BridgeWorks (from Paul):
- steady-state target: 500 tokens/sec per instance
- p95 target: <= 150ms for a ~1k token window
- sensitivity to cache misses (please include a cold-cache pass)

Suggested test matrix for the synthetic run (to discuss in the session):
- Warm-cache steady-state: 500 tps, run 10m to reach steady state
- Cold-cache ramp: 0 -> 600 tps over 5m, capture p50/p95/p99
- Spike test: 1s bursts to 1k tps for 30s to test autoscaling and graceful degradation

Please prepare the runbook (runbook-loadtest.xlsx) and a short slide with expected resource needs (GPU type, vCPU, mem, expected KV cache hit assumptions). If we need additional quota (extra GPU pool), flag the support ticket early — we27ll tie that to the mutual action plan.

Paul: I attached the runbook template we27ll use in the call. If you have a traffic trace or prompt samples, please drop them into the Drive link below before the session.

Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2B3Cxyz-drive-demo-prep
HubSpot: HS-983412

Cheers,
Olga

Attachment: runbook-loadtest.xlsx (Excel, template)
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Paul Nguyen <paul.nguyen@bridgeworks.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Apr 2027 15:20:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Architecture & perf deep-dive: confirm time and prep items

Looks good — I27ll own the architecture portion and the staging run. Quick notes:
- I27ve started a GPU quota request (JIRA: INF-3421) to reserve a small pool of A10G-equivalent instances for the synthetic runs. Screenshot attached.
- We27ll provision a staging endpoint with the same model binary (quantization profile to match production) and limited KV cache to measure cold/warm behavior.
- Karthik, can you produce an initial expected token/sec per GPU and the p95 baseline under warm vs cold conditions? I27ll add infra knobs to the runbook once we have those numbers.

Paul: see the ticket link in the runbook and the screenshot — I expect we27ll have quota in 24–36h if approvals go through.

Marcus
Marcus Lin
Platform Lead, Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwood.ai

Attachment: gpu-request-screenshot.png (PNG, 300KB)
